name: Sunnyside
one_liner: Sunnyside is an app and text-message program for cutting back on alcohol: a weekly drink plan, daily check-ins and a coach.
best_for: Adults who want to cut back on drinking rather than quit
People who would rather log drinks by text message than open an app
People who want light-touch accountability from a coach
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who get withdrawal symptoms (shakes, sweats, seizures) when they stop drinking: they need medical help to stop safely
People with severe alcohol use disorder who need treatment, not a moderation app
short_description: App and text-message program to drink less: weekly drink plan, daily tracking and coach messages. 15-day trial, then about $99/year.
long_description: Sunnyside (made by Cutback Coach, Inc.) is a US moderation program for people who want to drink less without necessarily quitting. You set a weekly drink plan, log drinks by text message or in the iOS or Android app, and get daily tips and messages from a coach. Reviews list plans at about $12 a month, $29 a quarter or $99 a year after a 15-day free trial, with a pricier premium tier that adds more hands-on coaching. The company has also launched Sunnyside Med, a separate online program that adds a naltrexone prescription for $99 a month (billed quarterly) plus a $50 intake fee. A 2024 study in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research looked at data from more than 45,000 Sunnyside users and found self-reported weekly drinking fell by about a third over 12 weeks; it had no comparison group, so it cannot show the program caused the drop. Its privacy policy says it does not share self-reported drinking data with ad partners but does share other data with advertising companies for interest-based ads.
patient_summary: You answer a short quiz, get a weekly drinking goal, and log drinks by text or in the app, with daily tips and messages from a coach. It is aimed at drinking less rather than quitting. After a 15-day free trial it costs about $99 a year (reviews also list $12 a month).

pricing.notes: Reviews list $12/month, $29/quarter or $99/year, and a premium coaching tier (about $298/year). No free version after the trial. Sunnyside Med (naltrexone plus coaching) is $99/month billed quarterly at $297, plus a $50 intake fee; HSA/FSA eligible, no insurance.

privacy.notes: Policy lists advertising companies as recipients for interest-based ads; says self-reported drinking data and SMS phone numbers are not shared with ad partners. Account and content deletion in the app.

seo.title: Sunnyside: Review & Pricing
seo.meta_description: Sunnyside helps you drink more mindfully with a weekly drink plan, tracking by app or text message, and access to human coaches, without requiring sobriety.

faqs.a: 15-day trial, then about $99.99/year. Prices were checked in October 2026 and can change, so confirm with Sunnyside before you sign up.

faqs.q: Can Sunnyside replace therapy or treatment?
faqs.a: No. Sunnyside is a self-help tool that can support your wellbeing or work alongside therapy, but it doesn't diagnose or treat conditions. If you're in crisis, call or text 988 in the US.
Sunnyside is available on iPhone and Android.
Weekly drink plans; Tracking by app or text; Coach messaging; Community; Progress dashboard.

clinical_trials.study: Self-reported drinking among Sunnyside users over 12 weeks

citation.title: Self-reported alcohol consumption during participation in a text messaging-based online drinking moderation platform

clinical_trials.outcome: Self-reported weekly drinks fell by about one third over 12 weeks, mostly in the first 6 weeks. Self-selected users, no control group, missing data grew over time; Sunnyside supplied data but says it did not run the analysis.

primary_uses: Logging drinks by text message or app

availability.note: Sold in the US; iOS and Android apps plus text messages.
